title: Teaching
text: I teach health professionals to make better decisions with evidence. Most of my students will become managers, analysts, clinicians, and executives rather than researchers, so I focus on asking the right question of the data, reading the answer critically, and explaining it clearly to the person who has to decide.

title: Teaching
text:
Value and Quality in Healthcare (MHIA 6160)
A graduate course I designed for the Master of Health Industry Administration program at the Schulich School of Business, York University, first offered in Winter 2027. It is built on three ideas:

A dual lens. Each module is examined from the public-system perspective (equity, the Canada Health Act, regulation) and the industry perspective (efficiency, innovation, fiscal sustainability).
Code-along R laboratories. Students work from provided scripts, adjust parameters, and interpret the output, building data literacy for leadership without becoming programmers. All software is free and open source.
A simulation capstone. Student teams respond to a simulated epidemic using DAEDALUS, an open-access model from the Jameel Institute at Imperial College London, and present their strategy to a mock national cabinet.

title: Cameron B. Chiarot, MBA, PhD
text:
I am a healthcare executive, educator, and health economist with 20 years of senior leadership experience in Canadian public-sector health organizations. I use quantitative modelling to examine health system resilience, access, and value, and educate health leaders to support informed, evidence-based decision-making.
Health systems frequently discuss access; however, they typically measure utilization. The gap between the two is where systems fail people, and it is where my work is focused.

Leadership
Senior leadership roles across hospitals, health authorities, and research institutes, encompassing capital programs valued at up to CAD $100 million, the development of new health facilities, and governance in the not-for-profit sector.


Research
Health system resilience to climate shocks in Western Province, Zambia, and the economics of the HPTN 071 (PopART) trial with Imperial College London. More on my research →


Teaching
Adjunct Professor at the Schulich School of Business, where I designed and teach Value and Quality in Healthcare (MHIA 6160), and Sessional Lecturer in the Master of Public Health program at the University of Waterloo. More on my teaching →

I am seeking leadership opportunities in applied research, innovation, and education across public agencies, health systems, research institutes, universities, and colleges. The best way to reach me is by email or LinkedIn.

title: Research
text: My research asks whether health systems deliver care to the people who need it, and how well they hold up under pressure. I distinguish potential access, the services people could in principle reach, from realized access, the services they actually use, and I model what drives the gap between the two: distance, cost, climate shocks, and the capacity of the system itself.

title: Research
text:
Current work
Health system resilience in Western Province, Zambia (University of Waterloo, 2025 – present). Using routine health information system data, I measure how floods, droughts, and other health system stressors affect the use of essential services, including maternal and child health care, and I develop methods to strengthen malaria surveillance data. This work grew out of my doctoral thesis, Health System Resilience for Climate Change Adaptation.
The economics of HIV care in the HPTN 071 (PopART) trial (Imperial College London, 2026 – present). With colleagues at Imperial College London, I model equity, economies of scale, and the costs of health care utilization in a cluster-randomized trial in Zambia and South Africa.

title: Research
text:
Methods
Frequentist and Bayesian modelling; econometrics, including interrupted time series and difference-in-differences; time-series forecasting; structural equation modelling; and geospatial analysis, including catchment-area and location-allocation methods. I work mainly in R.
